componentizejs.pinned_commit_note: Post-release maintenance commit on main; package.json version is still 0.21.0 at this commit (verified via GitHub contents API on 2026-07-14). The published git tag for 0.21.0 is a different, earlier commit (5be3a668d3c0612adf93592cbc8b91d4a6190c9d); both represent the same 0.21.0 release line. The npm-published 0.21.0 tarball (which has no recorded gitHead) is used as the operational reference install in tests/compat/reference/, since it is what an opt-in user would actually install.
componentizejs.value_shape_baseline_source: Documented public behavior (README.md/EXAMPLE.md of the pinned repository, https://github.com/WebAssembly/component-model canonical ABI conventions) plus empirical verification performed for this manifest (see verified_by_reference_run below). Not copied from any ComponentizeJS source file.

wasmtime_invoker_pin.status: matched exactly, via a scoped host-only Rust 1.91 toolchain
wasmtime_invoker_pin.note: tests/compat/runtime/invoker/Cargo.toml pins wasmtime/wasmtime-wasi/wasmtime-wasi-http to exact =42.0.1, matching this repository's own pin (see repository_pin_source). The published wasmtime 42.0.1 crate requires rustc >= 1.91.0 (edition 2024), newer than this repository's root rust-toolchain.toml (channel 1.88.0, pinned for producing wasm32-wasip1 artifacts); this is not a blocker because tests/compat/runtime/invoker is a standalone host-side test tool that produces no wasm32-wasip1 output and is never linked into StarlingMonkey itself. It carries its own nested tests/compat/runtime/invoker/rust-toolchain.toml pinning exact Rust 1.91.0 (profile=minimal, host-only), independently of and without changing the repository root's toolchain; rustup resolves the nearest rust-toolchain.toml by walking up from cwd, and both tests/compat/runtime/lib/run_bridge_tests.py's build_invoker() and tests/compat/reference/run-reference.mjs invoke cargo with an absolute cwd inside invoker/, so this is honored regardless of the caller's own working directory. See tests/compat/runtime/README.md's 'Wasmtime version' section for the exact API adaptations (invoker/src/main.rs) and verification commands.
wasmtime_invoker_pin.verified_by: cargo metadata (run from tests/compat/runtime/invoker) reports wasmtime/wasmtime-wasi/wasmtime-wasi-http all resolved to exact 42.0.1; rustc --version there reports 1.91.0. Both the real bridge (run-bridge-tests.sh) and reference (run-reference.mjs) suites were re-run to 11/11 against this exact pin; see git history for this repository's compat harness commits for the reproduced output.

verified_by_reference_run.description: Every fixture below except the two negative fixtures was actually componentized with the pinned npm package (@bytecodealliance/componentize-js@0.21.0, which required a portable Node.js >=22 since the environment's default Node 20.14 cannot load that package's native optional dependencies) and executed through Wasmtime -- specifically tests/compat/runtime/invoker's dynamic Component Model API on the official `wasmtime` Rust crate, without another component transpiler -- to record real observed reference values rather than assumed ones. The two negative fixtures were run through the same componentize() call to observe componentization-time behavior (no wasm execution involved for those two). This one-time verification pass is not part of normal CI; tests/compat/reference/ lets it be reproduced with one command (`npm install && node run-reference.mjs`).
verified_by_reference_run.environment_note: This repository does not depend on Node/npm normally; the verification pass above used a temporary, non-committed Node 22 install and is not required to build or test this repository. Direct Wasmtime execution ensures observed defects (see known_deviations componentizejs-u32-high-bit-defect) are attributable to ComponentizeJS itself, not to a second adapter.

bridge.description: Zig/WABT dispatch bridge (runtime/js_dispatch.cpp + runtime/js_dispatch.zig): a WABT-generated per-export Zig shell JSON-encodes its typed WIT arguments, calls starling_js_dispatch(), which JSON.parses them into a JS array and applies it as positional arguments to a same-named top-level export of the initialized top-level JS module, then JSON.stringifies the return value back across the boundary. A returned Promise traps rather than being awaited.

known_deviations.summary: WIT `none` arrives to the JS export as `null` in the current JSON bridge (Zig `std.json` serializes a Zig optional's null case as JSON `null`, and `JSON.parse` yields JS `null`), whereas the pinned ComponentizeJS reference lifts `none` as JS `undefined`. Both bridges accept `null` or `undefined` returned from JS as lowering to `none`.
known_deviations.evidence: tests/compat/fixtures/options + tests/compat/reference (see maybenumber/maybestring/maybepoint cases in expected/options.json)

known_deviations.summary: The pinned ComponentizeJS reference rejects a WIT-declared export that JavaScript does not implement (or implements as a non-function) at componentization time, with a message naming the missing/invalid export. The current Zig/WABT bridge resolves the JS export lazily by name on each call (see js_dispatch.cpp's JS_GetProperty/JS::IsCallable check), so the same mistake is only observed as a call-time trap, not a componentization-time failure: build-verified by actually building and componentizing both negative fixtures' reactors and invoking the missing/invalid export through Wasmtime (tests/compat/runtime), which traps rather than failing componentization. The wasm trap itself carries no message text (a bare `unreachable`); the descriptive "... is not a function" diagnostic is printed by the JS engine's own panic handler to the guest's stderr stream, which tests/compat/runtime/invoker captures alongside the trap for comparison.

Empirically, values of a plain `u32` argument/result at or above 2^31 (2147483648) did not round-trip correctly through the pinned ComponentizeJS 0.21.0 reference in this environment (e.g. echou32(4294967295) returned 4292870144, echou32(2147483648) returned 0), even in a minimal single-function isolated world. This was re-verified by invoking the real componentize-js output directly through Wasmtime (tests/compat/runtime/invoker), with no other transpiler in the call path, so the defect is attributable to ComponentizeJS/its embedded engine itself, not to a transpilation adapter. Root cause not diagnosed here (candidates include the embedded engine's own canonical-ABI numeric lifting/lowering); root-caused and either fixed upstream or worked around in a later phase. The current Zig/WABT bridge (runtime/js_dispatch.zig, which serializes numbers as JSON decimal text parsed by JS as an exact float64) has been build-verified unaffected: the actual reactor was built and its echou32 export invoked through Wasmtime for the same boundary values (0, 2147483647, 2147483648, 4294967295), all of which round-tripped correctly (see fixtures/numeric-primitives runtime_verification).
known_deviations.confidence: wasmtime-verified (defect, no transpiler adapter involved), build-verified (bridge unaffected)

known_deviations.summary: u64/s64 are not exercised by Phase 0 fixtures. ComponentizeJS lifts them as JS BigInt; the current JSON bridge round-trips them as JS Number via JSON text, which loses precision above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (2^53-1). Phase 1a is expected to move to a typed bridge with BigInt support.

A Promise-returned from a JS export traps synchronously (js_dispatch.cpp explicitly rejects JS::IsPromiseObject results) instead of being driven to completion, unlike the pinned ComponentizeJS reference which can synchronously drive Promise-returning exports to completion.
Every call boundary serializes arguments and results through JSON text rather than a typed SpiderMonkey JS::Value conversion.
Enums, flags, variants, results, resources, futures and streams are not represented by the bridge or by any Phase 0 fixture.

When a WIT world exports a named interface (e.g. `export api;` with `api` containing `add`), the pinned ComponentizeJS reference requires the JS module to export a matching namespace object (e.g. `export const api = { add, ... }`); it fails componentization otherwise with 'does not export an "<iface>" interface as expected by the world'. The current Zig/WABT bridge instead strips everything up to and including the last '#' in the canonical export name and looks up that bare name directly as a flat top-level export, regardless of interface qualification (see js_dispatch.cpp's `export_name.rfind('#')`), matching the existing tests/fixtures/js-dispatch.js fixture which uses flat exports under an interface-qualified world. Phase 0 fixtures therefore declare exports directly on `world js-exports { export name: func(...); }` (no named interface) so the same JS source is valid under both pipelines.

This is a deviation of the tests/compat/runtime harness itself, not of the underlying bridge: each fixture's original `tests/compat/fixtures/<id>/wit/world.wit` declares its exports directly on the world (flat top-level exports; see interface-export-flattening above). The pinned ComponentizeJS reference pipeline (tests/compat/reference/run-reference.mjs) componentizes that unmodified flat world.wit directly, so its componentized output's fixture functions are genuine flat top-level component exports. The real-bridge pipeline (tests/compat/runtime), however, cannot build the fixture's flat world directly against the actual StarlingMonkey js-dispatch host WIT (host-apis/wasi-0.2.10/wit/js-dispatch.wit), which requires the guest to export a named `starling:js/api` interface alongside the full WASI 0.2.10 import closure; tests/compat/lib/gen_bridge_wit.py therefore mechanically rewrites each fixture's flat exports into `interface api { ... } world js-exports { export api; }` under `package starling:js;` before building the reactor (see gen_bridge_wit.py's module docstring). The two pipelines' componentized artifacts therefore have genuinely different WIT export surfaces for the same fixture: the bridge's output exports its functions nested one level down, under the `starling:js/api` interface instance, while the reference's output exports the same functions flat at the component's top level. tests/compat/runtime/invoker's `resolve_func` deliberately searches both shapes (top-level first, then one level of nested interface instances) purely so one invoker/manifest can drive both pipelines by bare function name -- this is a pragmatic harness convenience, not evidence that the two componentized artifacts present an identical WIT interface. The 11/11 pass counts in this manifest validate call-level argument/result semantics parity between the pipelines; they do not validate WIT-surface/interface-shape parity, which is out of scope for Phase 0 and remains open (a future phase could close it by also wrapping the reference's WIT in a matching named interface, provided ComponentizeJS's own namespace-object export requirement -- see interface-export-flattening -- is satisfied).
